narrative: The model estimates an 85% probability that you will leave, so the promotion was denied because the organization is treating you as a high retention risk. The three strongest factors all pushed toward leaving. The most influential was that you reported other job opportunities while in this job: only 23.3% of employees predicted to stay said they had other opportunities, so this is a strong signal of possible departure. The second was your 6–10 years of total experience; that is more experience than the largest group of stayers, who have 1–5 years (50.4%), and it added upward pressure toward leaving. The third was your 1–5 years in the current organization; although this is common among stayers (51.2%), it still leaned toward leaving in your case. Before this becomes final, the organization should use it as a retention warning: discuss concrete promotion criteria and timing, ask what would make you stay, and review development gaps—especially since you did not find the training useful. You should clarify whether the external opportunities, experience level, or promotion path are driving your thinking, and what support or role change would keep you engaged.
